tool.name: open_redirect_check
tool.description:
Probe a URL for open-redirect vulnerabilities. Sweeps the redirect-shaped parameters in the URL with the standard 11-payload bypass cohort and detects attacker-host placement in 30x `Location` / `Content-Location` / `Refresh` headers, body `` redirects, and body `window.location` assignments. Standard pentest deliverable.
Methodology:
1. **Discover redirect-shaped params** in the target URL — names matched against a 40-name lexicon (`next`, `redirect`, `return`, `goto`, `dest`, `url`, `redirect_uri`, `callback`, `image_url`, `successurl`, etc.). If the URL has no redirect-shaped params, falls back to probing 6 default names appended to the URL. 2. **Replay each candidate parameter** with the 11-payload bypass cohort (direct https / direct http / protocol-relative / backslash / userinfo confusion / userinfo+# / subdomain confusion / query-bypass / encoded slash / javascript: scheme / data: scheme). 3. **Detect attacker host** in `Location` / `Content-Location` / `Refresh` headers, body ``, or body `window.location` assignment.
Severity tuning:
- **High** (CWE-601, open_redirect) — attacker host in `Location` / `Content-Location` / `Refresh` response header (3xx redirect or refresh). - **Medium** (CWE-601) — attacker host in body `` content URL or in `window.location` / `location.href` / `location.replace` assignment. - **Medium** (CWE-601) — `javascript:` or `data:` scheme reflected in a Location header (severity capped at medium because most browsers block 30x to javascript: now).
Per-param dedup: at most one finding per (param_name × severity) so an 11-payload cohort against a single vulnerable param produces ONE report. Per-probe verdicts still live in the result dict for the agent.
The matcher checks the netloc segment of the redirect target, not raw substring — so a session token containing `evil.example` characters in the response body doesn't false-positive. A `target.com.evil.example` netloc matches (suffix check); `target.com/evil.example` doesn't (it's a path on target.com).
Composes with cluster-A safety (auth-injection / exclude-path / rate-limit) automatically. Read-only: GET only, follow_redirects=False so the 30x decision is observable.
Each finding includes `description_plain` + `recommended_action` (maintain a server-side allow-list of redirect targets; reject any client-supplied target that isn't on the list; prefer relative paths over full URLs; treat `//host`, `\\host`, and userinfo forms as absolute URLs during validation, not relative paths). `verification_status=needs_review` since reflected attacker-host in the response is a strong signal but the agent should confirm victim-side browser behavior (some intermediate WAFs / browser mitigations block the redirect even when the server emits it).
Probe attacker host gets a unique random `strix-.evil.example` prefix per run for log auditability.

parameter.name: target_url
parameter.description: URL to probe. Bare hostnames are auto-prefixed with `https://`. If the URL has a query string, the tool looks for redirect-shaped param names in it. If the URL has no query string, the tool falls back to probing 6 default names appended to the URL. Examples: `https://app.example.com/login?next=/dashboard`, `https://app.example.com/oauth/callback?redirect_uri=...`, `https://app.example.com/logout` (default-fallback).

parameter.name: extra_param_names
parameter.description: Additional redirect-shaped param names to probe regardless of whether the URL already has them. Useful when the agent has discovered a non-standard redirect param via crawl analysis (e.g. `myredirect`, `forward_to`).

parameter.name: attacker_host
parameter.description: Override the base attacker host used in payloads (default `evil.example`). A unique random `strix-.` prefix is auto-prepended so probes are auditable in target logs and don't collide with any pre-existing references.

returns.description:
{success, target_url, target_host, attacker_host, probed_params, probes: [{param, label, class_, payload, status, evidence: {header_redirect, header_value, scheme_in_header, meta_refresh, window_location}, finding_severity}, ...], findings_emitted}.
The agent should verify high-severity findings by manually following the 30x with a browser-like client and confirming the final landing host is attacker-controlled. Some intermediate WAFs / browser mitigations block the actual redirect even when the server emits it.
